Done — the migration is finished and `node verify.js` passes.

**What was left on the old call:** 12 files, 36 call sites.

- `packages/accounts` — `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js`
- `packages/billing` — `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js`
- `packages/catalog` — `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js`
- `packages/orders` — `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js`
- `packages/support` — `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js`
- `packages/analytics` — `repo/cohort.js`

Each became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, keeping the same SQL string and the same params array — including the spread ones in the `update*` functions.

**Two things I deliberately did not touch:**

- `cache.query(...)` in the repo files. Same method name, different object — that's the cache, not the database. All 25 uses are unchanged.
- `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`, which still has 2 `db.query` calls. Vendored code gets replaced on upgrade, so editing it would just be lost.

I also left `db.query` itself in place in `lib/db.js`. Nothing in the app calls it now, so you can drop it whenever you like — but `verify.js` stubs it to catch runtime callers, so removing it would need that check updated too.
